# 1 Samuel Chapter 9 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 154v-155r | **Source Image:** 1SA_009_page_001.jpg, 1SA_009_page_002.jpg

---

**9:1** And-there-was a-man from-Benjamin, and-his-name [was] Kish son of-Abiel, son of-Zeror, son of-Becorath, son of-Aphiah, a-Benjaminite, a-mighty-man of-valor.

**9:2** And-to-him there-was a-son, and-his-name [was] Saul, a-young-man and-good, and-there-was-not a-man from-[the]-sons of-Israel more-handsome than-he; from-his-shoulder and-upward [he was]-taller than-all the-people.

**9:3** And-were-lost the-donkeys of-Kish, [the]-father of-Saul. And-said Kish to-Saul his-son, "Take, please, with-you one of-the-servants, and-arise, go, seek the-donkeys."

**9:4** And-he-passed through-[the]-hill-country of-Ephraim, and-he-passed through-[the]-land of-Shalishah, and-they-did-not find [them]. And-they-passed through-[the]-land of-Shaalim, and-[they were]-not [there]. And-he-passed through-[the]-land of-[the]-Benjaminites, and-they-did-not find [them].

**9:5** They came to-[the]-land of-Zuph, and-Saul said to-his-servant who [was] with-him, "Come, and-let-us-return, lest my-father cease from-the-donkeys and-be-anxious about-us."

**9:6** And-he-said to-him, "Behold, please, a-man of-God [is] in-this city, and-the-man [is] honored; all which he-says surely comes [to pass]. Now let-us-go there; perhaps he-will-tell us our-way upon which we-have-gone."

**9:7** And-said Saul to-his-servant, "But-behold, [if] we-go, then-what shall-we-bring to-the-man? For the-bread is-gone from-our-vessels, and-[there is]-no gift to-bring to-the-man of-God. What [is] with-us?"

**9:8** And-the-servant answered Saul again and-said, "Behold, there-is-found in-my-hand a-quarter of-a-shekel of-silver, and-I-will-give [it] to-the-man of-God, and-he-will-tell us our-way."

**9:9** (Formerly in-Israel, thus said the-man when-going to-inquire of-God: "Come and-let-us-go to the-seer [ha-ro'eh]." For the-prophet [navi] of-today was-called formerly the-seer [ha-ro'eh].)

**9:10** And-said Saul to-his-servant, "Your-word [is] good. Come, let-us-go." And-they-went to the-city where the-man of-God [was].

**9:11** They [were]-going-up the-ascent of-the-city, and-they found young-women going-out to-draw water. And-they-said to-them, "Is the-seer [ha-ro'eh] here?"

**9:12** And-they-answered them and-said, "He-is. Behold, before-you. Hurry now, for today he-came to-the-city, for [there is] a-sacrifice for-the-people today on-the-high-place [bamah].

**9:13** When-you-come to-the-city, so you-will-find him before he-goes-up to-the-high-place to-eat, for the-people will-not eat until he-comes, for he blesses the-sacrifice; afterward the-invited-ones eat. And-now go-up, for him — as-today you-will-find him."

**9:14** And-they-went-up to-the-city. They [were]-coming into-[the]-midst of-the-city, and-behold, Samuel [was]-coming-out toward-them to-go-up to-the-high-place.

**9:15** And-YHWH had-uncovered the-ear of-Samuel one day before-[the]-coming of-Saul, saying,

**9:16** "About-this time tomorrow I-will-send to-you a-man from-[the]-land of-Benjamin, and-you-shall-anoint him [as] leader [nagid] over my-people Israel, and-he-will-save my-people from-[the]-hand of-[the]-Philistines, for I-have-seen my-people, for their-cry has-come to-me."

**9:17** And-Samuel saw Saul, and-YHWH answered him, "Behold, the-man of-whom I-said to-you, 'This-one shall-restrain [ya'atsor] my-people.'"

**9:18** And-drew-near Saul to-Samuel in-[the]-midst of-the-gate and-said, "Tell me, please, where [is the]-house of-the-seer?"

**9:19** And-Samuel answered Saul and-said, "I [am] the-seer. Go-up before-me to-the-high-place, and-you-shall-eat with-me today, and-I-will-send-you-away in-the-morning, and-all that [is] in-your-heart I-will-tell you.

**9:20** And-as-for-the-donkeys, the-[ones]-lost to-you three days ago, do-not set your-heart upon-them, for they-have-been-found. And-to-whom [is] all the-desire of-Israel? Is-it-not to-you and-to-all the-house of-your-father?"

**9:21** And-answered Saul and-said, "Am-not I a-Benjaminite, from-the-smallest of-[the]-tribes of-Israel, and-my-clan the-least of-all the-clans of-[the]-tribe of-Benjamin? And-why have-you-spoken to-me according-to-this word?"

**9:22** And-took Samuel Saul and-his-servant and-brought-them to-the-chamber [lishkah] and-gave to-them a-place at-[the]-head of-the-invited-ones, and-they [were]-about thirty men.

**9:23** And-said Samuel to-the-cook, "Give the-portion which I-gave to-you, of-which I-said to-you, 'Set it aside with-you.'"

**9:24** And-raised-up the-cook the-thigh and-what-was-upon-it and-set [it] before Saul. And-he-said, "Behold, what-was-reserved is-set before-you; eat, for to-the-appointed-time it-was-kept for-you, saying, 'The-people I-have-invited.'" And-ate Saul with Samuel on-that day.

**9:25** And-they-came-down from-the-high-place to-the-city. And-he-spoke with Saul on the-roof.

**9:26** And-they-rose-early. And-it-was at-[the]-going-up of-the-dawn, and-called Samuel to-Saul on-the-roof, saying, "Arise, and-I-will-send-you-away." And-arose Saul, and-went-out [the]-two-of-them, he and-Samuel, to-the-outside.

**9:27** They [were]-going-down at-[the]-edge of-the-city, and-Samuel said to-Saul, "Say to-the-servant that-he-should-pass-on before-us" — and-he-passed-on — "but-you, stand at-this-time, and-I-will-cause-you-to-hear the-word of-God."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **9:1 — "mighty man of valor"** (גִּבּוֹר חַיִל): This phrase introduces Kish with military/aristocratic overtones. The same epithet is used for Boaz (Ruth 2:1) and Gideon (Judges 6:12).

2. **9:9 — Parenthetical gloss on "seer"**: The narrator explains that the older term *ro'eh* (seer) has been replaced by *navi* (prophet). This is a rare editorial aside that reveals the text's compositional layers.

3. **9:16 — nagid** (נָגִיד): Translated "leader" rather than "king" (*melek*). Samuel uses *nagid* for Saul's designated role — a term emphasizing military leadership under YHWH's authority rather than dynastic monarchy. The distinction is theologically significant.

4. **9:17 — ya'atsor** (יַעְצֹר): "shall restrain" — an unusual verb choice. Some read it as "shall rule/govern" but the root *ʿ-ts-r* fundamentally means "to hold back, restrain." EMET preserves the literal sense.

5. **9:20 — "all the desire of Israel"**: A cryptic statement. Samuel hints at kingship without naming it directly. The Hebrew *chemdah* (desire/precious thing) frames the monarchy as something longed-for.

— EMET
